reasons_add: Ibn ʿAṭiyya explicitly says the Prophet turns or presents himself toward the person.

Abū Ḥayyān reports an identification with Umayya together with the figures named in the occasion report. The account from ʿĀʾisha cited by al-Durr names Abū Jahl and ʿUtba among the Quraysh leaders being addressed.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya glosses the verb as turning or presenting oneself toward someone.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya names al-Aʿraj, al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Qatāda, ʿĪsā, and al-Aʿmash among those reading a light ṣād through deletion; Abū Ḥayyān also lists them and the majority of the seven, deriving the light form from yataṣaddā. Al-Nashr assigns the ungeminated ṣād to the remaining readers.

Al-Nashr assigns the geminated ṣād to the two Medinan readers and Ibn Kathīr; Ibn ʿAṭiyya names Ibn Kathīr and Nāfiʿ, and Abū Ḥayyān calls them the two sanctuary readers and explains assimilation of the tāʾ.

Ibn Jinnī explains Abū Jaʿfar's passive form as worldly adornment drawing the Prophet toward the wealthy man. Ibn ʿAṭiyya says concern for disbelievers causes the Prophet to turn toward them; Abū Ḥayyān specifies eagerness for this man's conversion.
Al-Durr cites another account from ʿĀʾisha: the Prophet was addressing Quraysh leaders including Abū Jahl and ʿUtba when Ibn Umm Maktūm arrived; the Prophet turned away, and the passage was revealed.

question: Where was Ibn Umm Maktūm at the time of the proposed encounter?

positions.position: He was in Medina while Umayya and al-Walīd were in Mecca, so they could not have been the men involved.
positions.reasons: Al-Qurṭubī, quoted by Abū Ḥayyān, objects to the identifications on this geographic basis.

positions.position: He was in Mecca before emigrating; all those figures were there when this Meccan sūra was revealed.
positions.reasons: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Qurṭubī's objection because Ibn Umm Maktūm was initially in Mecca and the sūra was revealed there.

question: Who was Ibn Umm Maktūm in this account?

positions.position: He was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sarḥ ibn Mālik ibn Rabīʿa al-Fihrī of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, Khadīja's cousin; Umm Maktūm was his paternal grandmother ʿĀtika.
positions.reasons: Abū Ḥayyān gives this name, lineage, kinship, and explanation of his designation.
